newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, U.S. to meet on insurance around Nov 15 - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. to meet on insurance around Nov 15 - MOF.

text.p: Senior Japanese and U.S. officials will meet around November 15 to discuss their dispute about deregulating Japan's insurance market, Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday.
However, there has been no decision yet concerning a minister-level meeting, Kubo said.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, will meet Ira Shapiro of the U.S. Trade Representative's (USTR) Office in San Francisco for the talks, Kubo said.

Minister-level talks may take place during the meeting of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum members, which is due to be held in the Philippines at the end of November, he said. Various international conferences will be held in Asia around that time, and Kubo added that acting USTR Charlene Barshefsky may be able to visit Tokyo when she attends such conferences.
Japan and the United States have already started working-level talks on whether such a visit by Barshefsky would be possible, he said.
"I think the insurance talks will start rolling after the U.S. presidential elections," he said.

Asked about the impact of the failure of non-bank financial institutions, such as Nichiei Finance Co Ltd's filing for liquidation on Tuesday, on the financial system, Kubo said problem loans at non-bank institutions should be dealt with by related financial firms.
"It would be a big problem if the impact of non-bank institutions' failures spread throughout the financial industry. We would like to keep careful watch over the situation," he said.
